neighbours.label: a prohibition verb ending a sequence of sanctions ('suspended and then banned')
fire: The newspapers were first censored and then banned outright in 1974.
The party was dissolved, its leaders jailed, and its symbols banned.
Opposition groups were restricted and later outlawed by decree.
The union was suspended and eventually banned by the junta.
Books by the poet were removed from libraries and then banned.
The church was harassed for years and finally prohibited in 1938.
Strikes were discouraged and then forbidden under the new law.
The movement was monitored, infiltrated and eventually banned.
quiet: The newspapers were first printed and then sold outright in 1974.
The party was founded, its leaders elected, and its symbols designed.
Opposition groups were formed and later merged by agreement.
The union was created and eventually expanded by the workers.
Books by the poet were added to libraries and then reprinted.
The church was restored for years and finally reopened in 1938.
Strikes were common and then rare under the new law.
The movement was growing, organizing and eventually winning.

notes: broad flag; probe: 'suspended and then banned' 0.58, 'later banned by the government' 0.10
